question: Compare maize and soybean: what does each need?

rows.a: Mean temperature during growth: optimal 18-33 °C, tolerated 10-47 °C.
rows.b: Mean temperature during growth: optimal 20-33 °C, tolerated 10-38 °C.

rows.a: Annual rainfall: optimal 600-1200 mm, tolerated 400-1800 mm.
rows.b: Annual rainfall: optimal 600-1500 mm, tolerated 450-1800 mm.

rows.a: Soil depth: optimal medium (50-150 cm); tolerated shallow (20-50 cm).
rows.b: Soil depth: optimal medium (50-150 cm); tolerated shallow (20-50 cm).

rows.a: Soil fertility: optimal high; tolerated low.
rows.b: Soil fertility: optimal high; tolerated low.

rows.b: Salinity: optimal low (<4 dS/m); tolerated medium (4-10 dS/m).

EcoCrop gives one envelope per species, not per variety, and has no year of publication for a single record.

answer:
Maize and soybean share similar broad climatic and soil requirements while differing in specific optimal ranges [S1]. For temperature, maize has an optimal mean temperature of 18-33 °C and tolerates 10-47 °C, whereas soybean prefers an optimal temperature of 20-33 °C and tolerates 10-38 °C [S1].

Regarding water, maize requires an annual rainfall of 600-1200 mm with a tolerance of 400-1800 mm, while soybean needs an optimal 600-1500 mm and tolerates 450-1800 mm [S1]. Both crops thrive best in soils with high fertility and a medium depth of 50-150 cm [S1].

For soil pH, maize performs best at 5-7 and tolerates 4.5-8.5, while soybean prefers a narrower range of 5.5-6.5 and tolerates 4.5-8.4 [S1]. Soybean additionally specifies an optimal medium organic soil texture and well-drained conditions [S1].
